text: I am really sorry you are hurting this much. You matter, and you do not have to go through this alone. Please talk to someone right now: call 114 (free, Rwanda Biomedical Centre) or go to the nearest health center or hospital. If you are in danger right now, call 112. If you can, tell a person you trust near you, such as a family member, friend, teacher or nurse, and stay with them. I am an information tool and cannot give you the support a real person can.

I am sorry this happened to you. It is not your fault, and you deserve to be safe. You can get help: call 3512 (gender-based violence, free) or 116 (child helpline, free), or call 112 if you are in danger now. Isange One Stop Centres (call 3029) and health facilities give medical, counselling and legal support. If it happened in the last 72 hours, go to a health facility as soon as you can: there is medicine to lower the chance of HIV and emergency pills to prevent pregnancy. Please tell an adult you trust.

This could be serious. Please go to the nearest health facility or hospital now, or ask someone to take you. You can call 114 or the ambulance on 912. Do not wait. If someone is unconscious or cannot stand up, call for help immediately. I cannot give medical treatment through this tool.

I am sorry, I cannot tell you what illness you have. That needs a health worker to examine you and do tests. Please go to a health center for testing and treatment. Many problems are easy to treat when found early, and a health worker can answer your questions privately and without judging you. You can also ask me general questions, for example about signs of STIs or how HIV testing works.
I am Intyoza. I can only help with questions about growing up, periods, relationships, contraception, pregnancy, STIs and HIV. What would you like to know?

I am not sure about this, and I do not want to give you wrong information. Please ask a nurse or health worker at your nearest health center, or call 114. You can also ask me another question about growing up, periods, contraception, pregnancy, STIs, HIV or relationships. If you or someone else is in danger, hurt or feeling unsafe, call 112 now, or call 114 (health), 116 (child helpline) or 3512 (gender-based violence).
This is general health information and does not replace a health worker. We do not ask your name and do not save your questions.
For personal advice or tests, please visit your nearest health center or call 114.

I am sorry, I cannot give medicine doses or ways to end a pregnancy, because this can be dangerous without a health worker. Please speak to a nurse or pharmacist at your nearest health center, or call 114. If you are bleeding heavily, in severe pain or feeling unsafe, call 112 or go to a hospital now.
